analysis.title: Why Crypto Needs Its Own S&P 500: The Coinbase 50 Index
key_insights: MarketVector argues the Coinbase 50 Index (COIN50) should be the benchmark for the whole digital asset market, the way the S&P 500 is for US equities. Spot bitcoin ETFs hold more than $100bn, and the SEC now allows multi-asset crypto products to list under generic standards.

Bitcoin is capped at 50% of COIN50 at every quarterly rebalance. Its share of crypto market value has ranged from 38% to 72% since 2021 and is about 60% now, so the paper calls a bitcoin-only allocation a bet that the rest of the market stays irrelevant.

Leadership rotates. Only 15 of the January 2018 top 100 coins are still in the top 100, and only 3 of the top 10 (Bitcoin, Ether, XRP) remain in the top 10. About 64% of a top-100 cohort survives one year and 25% survives five.
COIN50 made 26 constituent additions in the last eight quarters, including Morpho, Ethena, Aptos, Sei and Flare. Bittensor entered in February 2026 and left in May.

Stablecoin supply grew from $34.5bn in January 2021 to $299bn in October 2026. Adjusted stablecoin volume was about $9 trillion in 2025, up 87% y/y (a16z). Ethereum hosts 54% of supply and Solana 5%, so about 60% of the float sits on networks held in COIN50.
Tokenized money-market and Treasury funds grew from $3.5bn in January 2024 to $34.3bn. Ethereum hosts 44.5% of tokenized funds and stocks, Solana 9.4%, Stellar 9.3% and Avalanche 3.4%.

AI-agent payments (x402 standard, contributed to the Linux Foundation in April 2026) are treated as an option rather than a driver. Some reported volume is test traffic. AI tokens NEAR, Render and Fetch.ai are 0.7% of the index.
Per the paper, 43% of COIN50, or 88% of the non-bitcoin weight, is exposure to stablecoin and tokenization infrastructure.

Size premium is negative once liquidity is required. MarketVector's Large Cap index compounded at 56% a year since 2014 (Sharpe 0.83). Mid and Small Cap compounded at about 33% with volatility above 90%, and liquidity-screened small caps lost 19% a year.

Since 31 Dec 2020 COIN50 returned +223.5% vs +191.2% for bitcoin and +238.2% for ether, with volatility of 63.0% vs 57.1% and 77.1% and a maximum drawdown of -78.3% vs -76.7% and -79.3%. Data before the 12 Nov 2024 launch is simulated.

Live performance since the 12 Nov 2024 launch to 21 Oct 2026 is -15.7% for COIN50, vs -4.2% for bitcoin and -23.2% for ether. COIN50 trailed bitcoin in 2025 (-16.6% vs -6.5%) and 2026 YTD (-11.2% vs -3.4%).

A back-tested 60/35/5 portfolio with COIN50 returned 11.2% a year with return/risk of 0.95, vs 10.7% and 0.90 with bitcoin and 8.7% and 0.81 for a 60/40. Maximum drawdown was -23.4% vs -20.8% for 60/40. The test excludes fees, costs and taxes.
COIN50 weekly correlation was 0.27 to US equities and 0.03 to US bonds. Bitcoin and ether together are 77.6% of the index, with bitcoin at 50.87% and ether at 26.70%.

Regulatory backdrop: the GENIUS Act (July 2025) takes effect by January 2027, the SEC approved generic listing standards for commodity-based ETPs in September 2025, and a joint SEC-CFTC release in March 2026 set a five-category token taxonomy.

Methodology: Coinbase-listed spot assets, a fundamental screen, 360-day seasoning, market-cap weighting, quarterly reviews (Feb, May, Aug, Nov) with a 41-60 buffer, and VWAP pricing. The index is owned by Coinbase and administered by MarketVector under IOSCO principles.
crypto_views: US spot bitcoin ETFs held about $106bn in mid-October 2026. The first US multi-asset spot crypto ETFs hold ten assets or fewer.
Bitcoin dominance is about 60% as of 21 Oct 2026. It was 92% in 2016, 33% in January 2018, and has moved between 72% and 38% since 2021.
The paper counts 2,309 tokens tracked since 2013, with 59 above $1bn in market value in September 2026.
COIN50 top weights as of 21 Oct 2026: BTC 50.87%, ETH 26.70%, XRP 7.67%, SOL 5.57%, DOGE 1.15%, LINK 0.83%, ADA 0.74%, NEAR 0.61%.
The paper expects index weight to spread beyond bitcoin as stablecoins, tokenization and AI payments grow. This is the author's expectation, not a data point.
Stablecoins are excluded from COIN50 by design because they are dollar-pegged. The index holds the networks they settle on.

trade_ideas.description: Core crypto allocation via a broad index (COIN50) instead of bitcoin alone. A 5% sleeve funded from the bond portion of a 60/40 portfolio, rebalanced quarterly.
trade_ideas.rationale: Back-test shows return/risk of 0.95 vs 0.81 for 60/40 and 0.90 with bitcoin, with maximum drawdown up less than three points.
trade_ideas.risk: The back-test is hypothetical, excludes fees, costs and taxes, and includes simulated index data before 12 Nov 2024. The disclosures cite material risk including total loss.

risk_factors: COIN50 data before its 12 Nov 2024 launch is simulated, so most of the performance record is back-tested.
Drawdowns match bitcoin's. COIN50's maximum drawdown was -78.3% since 2020.
Since live launch COIN50 has trailed bitcoin (-15.7% vs -4.2%), and it trailed in bitcoin-led years 2023-2026.
Some reported AI-agent payment volume is test traffic, and usage is early.
The paper's authors benefit from the index: Coinbase owns COIN50 and MarketVector earns licensing fees. The paper is labelled for informational and advertising purposes.
The disclosures cite risk of total loss and possible illiquidity for crypto and digital assets.
vol_and_positioning: COIN50 annualised volatility is 63.0%, between bitcoin at 57.1% and ether at 77.1%. Weekly correlation to COIN50 is 0.90 for bitcoin and 0.91 for ether.
Measured monthly, COIN50 captured 112% of bitcoin's up months and 107% of its down months.
Small Cap crypto is still 97% below its all-time high.

tension_points.bull_case: COIN50 returned +223.5% vs +191.2% for bitcoin since December 2020 and lifted a 60/40 portfolio's return/risk to 0.95 vs 0.90 with bitcoin. It captured 112% of bitcoin's up months, and broadening years such as 2021 favour it.
tension_points.bear_case: Most of the record is simulated before the 12 Nov 2024 launch. Live since launch COIN50 is -15.7% vs -4.2% for bitcoin, and it trailed bitcoin in 2025 and 2026 YTD. Maximum drawdown is similar to bitcoin's (-78.3% vs -76.7%), and it captured 107% of bitcoin's down months.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Continued bitcoin-led years: the paper says COIN50 trailed bitcoin in bitcoin-led years 2023-2026, so persistent bitcoin dominance near or above 60% would keep the gap.

theme_stances.key_argument: A rules-based, quarterly-reconstituted 50-coin index captures the whole crypto market and the networks behind stablecoins and tokenization, without picking winners.
theme_stances.evidence: Bitcoin is the anchor, not the whole market.

theme_stances.key_argument: Stablecoins and tokenized funds are growing on networks other than Bitcoin, and COIN50 holds those networks.
theme_stances.evidence: the real-world uses of crypto are growing on networks other than Bitcoin
